Over the past decade, Europe’s neobanks have burned through billions in VC money chasing growth.



Yet one neobank has quietly defied the playbook. Amsterdam-based Bunq is profitable, operates across Europe with a full banking licence and has amassed millions of users — all without raising VC funding.



But at home in the Netherlands, private equity-backed Bunq’s rise has been anything but low-profile. Dutch media have scrutinised its intense working culture, alongside allegations around lax financial crime controls and the misuse of customer data.
